## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix mixed-case writes so callers can retrieve and expire entries using the cache’s case-insensitive keys.

## Changes

The pull request adds `Cache.set`, raises the default TTL from 60 to 300 seconds, and adds tests for retrieval, expiration, and the default TTL constant.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Normalize keys before storing entries — After `set("Alpha", 1)`, `get("Alpha")` returns `None` because `set` stores `"Alpha"` and `get` looks up `"alpha"`. — Mixed-case writes are unreachable through the public API, and lookups never remove those entries after expiration.

## Suggestions

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Expire entries at their deadline — An entry written by `Cache().set("alpha", 1)` at monotonic time 1000 is still returned at 1300 because `get` checks `expires < time.monotonic()`. — A lookup at the expiration timestamp returns a stale value. — Fix: Use `<=` at `app/cache.py:21` and extend `test_entries_expire` to exercise the deadline.
- tests/test_cache.py:18 — tests — Verify the default TTL through cache behavior — If `Cache()` expires entries after 60 seconds while `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL` remains 300, `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` still passes because it only checks the constant. — The suite would miss a regression that shortens the default cache lifetime. — Fix: Extend `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` to observe expiration using the clock control in `test_entries_expire`.
- app/cache.py:7 — comments — Qualify the five-minute TTL as the default — For `Cache(ttl=1)`, the comment “Entries expire 300 seconds after they are written” gives the wrong lifetime because `set` computes the deadline with `time.monotonic() + self._ttl`. — Callers reading the comment get the wrong expiration interval for caches configured with a custom TTL.
